analysis.note: Predicate adjective qualifying the supplied ātmā; privative a- form, not treated here as an inflected compound.
Pronominal form ayam; subject is identified by the commentary as ātmā.
Predicate adjective qualifying ayam/ātmā; privative a- form.
Pronominal form ayam, again referring to ātmā.
Predicate adjective qualifying ayam/ātmā; understood by the commentary through avikriyatva, absence of transformation.
Pronominal form ayam, referring to ātmā.
“In this way”; Śaṅkara glosses it as yathokta-prakāreṇa.
ktvā-gerund/converb: “having known.” In the printed viditvainaṃ, viditvā + enam gives viditvainam by vowel sandhi.
Accusative singular pronoun, the enam-form of idam; Śaṅkara glosses enam as ātmānam. In viditvainaṃ the initial e is absorbed in the preceding ai by vowel sandhi.
Negates the infinitive construction na anuśocitum arhasi. In nānuśocitum, na + anuśocitum coalesces to nānuśocitum.

verification.detail: avyaya not in kosha or MW

analysis.note: Present active, 2nd singular; with infinitive and negation: “you ought not / are not fit to.”

justifications.decision: The repeated demonstrative ayam is translated as “this Self,” because Śaṅkara explicitly supplies ātmā with the predicates.
options_considered: ayam = this body/person presently under discussion
ayam = this Self, the subject of the teaching
justifications.chosen: ayam throughout refers to the Self (ātmā), not to the body or to an unspecified person.

evidence.quote: avyaktaḥ sarva-karaṇāviṣayatvāt na vyajyata iti avyakto 'yam ātmā |
evidence.translation: Because it is not an object of any instrument, it is not manifested; therefore this Self is avyakta.
But this Self, because it is not within the range of the senses, is acintya.
Because of being without modification, this Self is called avikārya.

justifications.decision: The word is not taken as the Sāṃkhya technical noun ‘the Unmanifest’ or as merely ‘undeveloped’; Śaṅkara derives the sense from na vyajyate and sarva-karaṇāviṣayatva.
justifications.chosen: avyakta is “unmanifest/imperceptible,” in the sense of not being objectified by any instrument of cognition.

evidence.quote: avyaktaḥ sarva-karaṇāviṣayatvāt na vyajyata iti avyakto 'yam ātmā |
evidence.translation: Avyakta: because it is not an object of any instrument; it is not manifested, hence this Self is avyakta.

justifications.decision: The translation avoids “not to be thought about” as a prescription; Śaṅkara presents an epistemic reason for its being beyond thought.
justifications.chosen: acintya is “inconceivable/beyond thought,” because thought has sense-objects as its field and the Self is not a sense-object.

evidence.quote: ataeva acintyo 'yam | yad dhi indriya-gocaras tac cintā-viṣayatvam āpadyate | ayaṃ tv ātmā anindriya-gocaratvāt acintyaḥ |
evidence.translation: Therefore this is acintya. Whatever is within the range of the senses becomes an object of thought; but this Self, because it is not within the range of the senses, is acintya.

justifications.decision: The commentary ties avikārya to absence of vikāra, contrasting the Self with milk transformed into curd and then explaining it by niravayavatva and avikriyatva.
options_considered: not to be altered as a gerundive prohibition
unmodifiable because not subject to transformation
justifications.chosen: avikārya is “unmodifiable/unchangeable,” specifically because the Self is avikriya, not subject to transformation and without parts.

evidence.quote: ataeva avikāryaḥ, yathā kṣīraṃ dadhyātañcanādinā vikāri na tathā ayam ātmā |
evidence.translation: Therefore it is avikārya: as milk is transformed by curdling agents, this Self is not so.
And because it is without parts, it is without modification.
Because of being without modification, this Self is called avikārya.

justifications.decision: The commentary fixes both the scope of evam and the referent of enam, and it construes the result as the impropriety of grieving over agency and slaughter.
options_considered: evam = in the manner just taught; enam = this Self
justifications.chosen: tasmāt evaṃ viditvā enam means “therefore, having known this Self in this way,” with evam = yathokta-prakāreṇa and enam = ātmānam.

evidence.quote: tasmāt evaṃ yathokta-prakāreṇa enam ātmānaṃ viditvā tvaṃ na anuśocitum arhasi hantāham eṣām, mayaite hanyanta iti ||bhgs_2.25||
evidence.translation: Therefore, having known this Self in this way, in the manner stated, you ought not to grieve, thinking ‘I am their slayer; by me these are slain.’

justifications.decision: With an infinitive, arhasi has the modal sense of fitness/obligation; Śaṅkara repeats the construction directly with tvaṃ and explains the false basis of grief.
options_considered: you do not deserve grief as an object
you ought not / are not fit to grieve
justifications.chosen: na anuśocitum arhasi is rendered “you ought not to grieve,” not merely “you cannot grieve.”

evidence.quote: tvaṃ na anuśocitum arhasi hantāham eṣām, mayaite hanyanta iti
evidence.translation: You ought not to grieve, thinking ‘I am their slayer; by me these are slain.’

translation: This Self is unmanifest (avyakta); this Self is inconceivable (acintya); this Self is said to be unmodifiable (avikārya). Therefore, having known this Self in this way, you ought not to grieve.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind rendering might take avyakta as a generic metaphysical ‘Unmanifest’ or prakṛti; Śaṅkara instead makes it the Self’s non-objectifiability by all instruments of cognition.
It might translate acintya simply as “unthinkable” without the reason that thought depends on sense-range, from which the Self is excluded.
It might render avikārya as only “invariable” or as a passive gerundive “not to be changed”; Śaṅkara glosses it through avikriyatva, niravayavatva, and the contrast with milk becoming curd.
It might leave enam as a vague “him/this”; Śaṅkara identifies it as ātmānam and ties the prohibition of grief to the mistaken thought “I am the slayer; these are slain by me.”
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 gives enam as enad_SAM; vidyut-prakriya rejects enad Pum/Dvitiya/Eka for enam, deriving enadam instead, so the lemma/stem is corrected to idam while keeping Pum/Dvitiya/Eka.
ByT5 gives anuśocitum as anuśuc_In; per the requested format this is normalized to bare root śuc with prefix anu and analyzed as an avyaya infinitive, not a finite verb.
ByT5 leaves tasmāt without explicit morphology; it is analyzed here as an indeclinable adverbial ablative, “therefore,” in accordance with its use and Śaṅkara’s tasmāt evaṃ gloss.

For surface_in_sandhi, fused vowel-sandhi strings are split into their printed substrings: viditvā/enam appears as viditvai/naṃ, and na/anuśocitum as nā/nuśocitum; the pausal surfaces give the actual lexical forms.
mula: avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam avikāryo 'yam ucyate | tasmād evaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitum arhasi

ataeva avikāryaḥ, yathā kṣīraṃ dadhyātañcanādinā vikāri na tathā ayam ātmā |
